Cook the vegetables according to package directions. If you purchase the steam bag, microwave the bag according to package directions and your microwave.

Mix the sour cream and honey mustard in a small bowl. Portion out 1 cup of vegetables in a bowl, layer garden burger on top and drizzle with sour cream/honey mustard mixture. Mix all together and enjoy!
hints: Look for frozen garden or vegetable burgers with the lowest amount of sodium. The recipe was tested with Morningstar® Garden Veggie Burger.
Any low potassium mixed vegetables or one single vegetable will work as well. Steam bag frozen vegetables are convenient and low in sodium. Try broccoli, cauliflower, mixed corn, green beans, etc.
Look for plain honey mustard or low-sodium varieties.

title: Buttercream Fruit Torte
description: Buttercream Fruit Torte is a kidney-friendly company dessert, rich in flavor and calories but so good you’ll want to share this low potassium recipe.
ingredients: 20 ounces canned juice packed, crushed pineapple
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F.
Melt 1/2 cup butter; combine with graham cracker crumbs and granulated sugar. Reserve 1/4 cup crust mixture for later use.
Press remaining mixture into an ungreased 9” x 13” pan.
Bake for 15 minutes; place pan in refrigerator to chill.
Whip together remaining 1 cup softened butter, powdered sugar, salt, vanilla and creamer until fluffy.
Spread filling mixture over chilled crust. Chill about 15 minutes.
Drain pineapple; slice strawberries. Spread pineapple and strawberries over filling. Chill for 30 minutes.
Before serving spread whipped topping over fruit. Sprinkle with reserved 1/4-cup graham cracker crust mixture.
hints: One stick of butter equals 1/2 cup.
One pint basket fresh strawberries yields 2 cups of sliced berries.

title: Vegetable Upma
description: Vegetable Upma is a kidney-friendly dish typically served at breakfast, but your family will love this grain-vegetable dish at lunch or dinner too.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Cream of Wheat® quick cooking cereal, uncooked
steps: Chop cashew nuts. Dice onion, carrot and tomato. Chop cilantro and jalapeno pepper. Grate ginger root.

Heat vegetable oil in a wok on the stove top over medium to high heat. When oil starts changing its color, add mustard seeds. When mustard seeds start to pop, turn the heat to medium low and add split chick peas (Chana dahl) and black beans (urad dahl). Stir the ingredients with a wooden spoon and add chopped cashew nuts. Fry until the peas and cashew nuts turn golden brown. Add cumin.
Add onion and saute to golden brown. Add tomatoes, carrots, peas, curry leaves, cilantro and ginger and cook until tomatoes soften.
Add cream of wheat and cook for 2-3 minutes.

Heat water to a boil. Add salt and stir in boiling water without forming lumps. Mixture becomes semi-solid consistency. Keep stirring until the water evaporates. Turn the heat to low and close the lid and cook for 3-4 minutes.
Turn the heat off. Sprinkle lemon juice and fluff with a fork. Divide into 2 portions and serve.
hints: Chana dahl, Urad dahl, mustard seeds, cumin and curry leaves are available at an Indian grocery store.
Upma is a well known breakfast dish in South India. In addition to semolina (farina, Cream of Wheat®), upma contains seasonings and vegetables.

title: Super Tuesday Shrimp
description: Protein lovers, your attention please! Shrimp and steak get the star treatment in this recipe by DaVita renal dietitian, Carol from California. Super Tuesday Shrimp is kidney-friendly and easy to make with Carol’s step-by-step cooking instructions. Simple, snappy and sensational!
ingredients: 1/4 cup sun dried tomatoes in oil
steps: Cook pasta according to package instructions, omitting salt. Drain and set aside.
Mince onion and garlic. Shell and devein shrimp.
Sauté onion and garlic in oil until lightly brown.
Add sun dried tomatoes, shrimp and pea pods.
Cook until shrimp change color (but pea pods remain crunchy).
Mix shrimp and pasta.
Sprinkle feta cheese on top and serve.
hints: Four ounces of dry pasta yields 2 cups cooked.
Frozen shrimp can be substituted for fresh shrimp.

title: Cranberry Dip with Fresh Fruit
description: Cranberry Dip with Fresh Fruit is a kidney-friendly snack that is low in potassium and is a great way to get vitamins and fiber from fruit. The DaVita renal dietitian team brings your this tasty party food recipe to enjoy with friends or as a snack on your own.
serving_size: 2 tablespoons dip, 2 slices apple, 2 slices pear and 3 pineapple chunks
steps: Place sour cream, cranberry sauce, nutmeg and ginger in a food processor and process until well mixed. Remove to a small bowl.
Cut pineapple into bite-size pieces. Cut apples and pears into 12 slices each. Toss apple and pear slices with lemon juice to prevent browning.
Arrange fruit on platter with dip bowl in the middle. Chill until ready to serve.
hints: Refrigerate leftover dip for up to 3 days.

title: Cranberry Muffins
description: This Cranberry Muffins recipe by DaVita dietitian Bonnie from Texas is modified for the kidney diet from a recipe she found in Better Homes and Garden® Cookbook.
ingredients: 1 cup fresh or frozen cranberries coarsely chopped
steps: Preheat oven to 400° F. Grease twelve 2-1/2″ muffin cups or line with baking cups; set aside.
To prepare streusel topping, combine 3 tablespoons of the flour, brown sugar and cinnamon in a bowl. Cut in 2 tablespoons butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs; set aside.
To prepare muffins, combine remaining flour, sugar, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl. Make a well in the center of the flour mixture; set aside.
In another bowl whisk egg, juice and oil together. Pour egg mixture all at once into flour mixture. Stir just until moistened (batter should be lumpy). Fold in chopped cranberries.

Spoon batter into prepared muffin cups, filling each 2/3 full. Sprinkle streusel topping over muffin batter in cups. Bake for 18 to 20 minutes or until golden and a wooden toothpick inserted in centers comes out clean.
Cool in muffin cups on a wire rack for 5 minutes. Remove from muffin cups; serve warm.
hints: Streusel topping is optional. Adds 2 grams fat and 2 grams carbohydate per muffin.
Freeze or refrigerate leftover muffins. Heat for 10 to 20 seconds in the microwave before serving.
